tipFakeUAOnAllRequestTypes.message: Fake UA on all request types

tipOpenTabsPickUpAUseragentSwitchImmedia.message: Open tabs pick up a useragent switch immediately, without a page reload

tipApplySwitchesToOpenTabsInstantly.message: Apply switches to open tabs instantly

tipAsksBeforeSwitchingBackToTheDefaultUs.message: Asks before switching back to the default useragent

tipAskForConfirmationBeforeSwitchingToTh.message: Ask for confirmation before switching to the default useragent

tipAsksBeforeTheFactoryResetClearsAllSet.message: Asks before the factory reset clears all settings, rules and the toolbar icon state

tipAskForConfirmationBeforeTheFactoryRes.message: Ask for confirmation before the factory reset

tipShowTheBackArrowInTheHeaderOfThe.message: Show the back arrow in the header of the settings, custom useragents and custom domains tabs — the home button in the footer already returns to the main view

tipShowTheBackArrowInThePanelHeaders.message: Show the back arrow in the panel headers

tipReopenThePopupOnTheLastOpenView.message: Reopen the popup on the last open view

tipWhenTheFakeBrowserHasNoVendorOfIts.message: When the fake browser has no vendor of its own (Firefox and friends), keep this browser's real vendor visible — useful only on sites that trust their own engine's vendor; off keeps the disguise complete

tipKeepTheRealVendorVisibleWhenTheFakeBr.message: Keep the real vendor visible when the fake browser sends none

tipCleansPastedSavedAndImportedUseragent.message: Cleans pasted, saved and imported useragent strings before the rules engine sees them: printable characters only, no line breaks, capped at 512 — a broken string can no longer disable switching; off hands strings over untouched

tipCleanPastedAndImportedStringsBeforeTh.message: Clean pasted and imported strings before the engine applies them

tipTintsTheDescriptionHeaderStripsTheBac.message: Tints the description header strips, the back arrows and the active mode chips in every tab, including the footer status line

tipReturnTheHeaderColorToTheThemeDefault.message: Return the header color to the theme default

tipPickTheColorOfTheDescriptionHeaderStr.message: Pick the color of the description header strips

tipTheFooterStatusStripTallOrShortHeight.message: The footer status strip: tall or short height and plain coloring on the left, and the checkbox on the right shows or hides the strip entirely

tipTallerStripWithTheInnerShineOfTheSett.message: Taller strip with the inner shine of the settings rows

tipStripTheBackgroundColorPlainCellWithA.message: Strip the background color: plain cell with a thin border — composes with tall or short

tipTypeOrPasteAUseragentString.message: Type or paste a useragent string

tipSaveThisStringToTheSavedUseragentsLis.message: Save this string to the saved useragents list below

tipTheUseragentOverrideCurrentlyAppliedT.message: The useragent override currently applied to this tab by This-tab mode

tipRemoveThisTabSUseragentOverrideTheTab.message: Remove this tab's useragent override — the tab returns to the global useragent

tipSavedUseragentStringsApplyTheSelected.message: Saved useragent strings: apply the selected one, load it into the editor, or remove it

tipApplyTheSelectedStringToEveryTabOrTo.message: Apply the selected string — to every tab, or to this tab only, as chosen in Settings

tipLoadTheSelectedStringIntoTheEditorAbo.message: Load the selected string into the editor above

tipWhatThisPageCurrentlyReportsAsItsUser.message: What this page currently reports as its useragent — use it to check that your switch took effect

tipCopyTheDetectedUseragentToTheClipboar.message: Copy the detected useragent to the clipboard

tipChooseWhetherTheUseragentAppliesOnlyO.message: Choose whether the useragent applies only on the listed domains, or on every site except the listed ones

tipExclusiveTheUseragentAppliesOnEverySi.message: Exclusive: the useragent applies on every site except the domains in the list below

tipInclusiveTheUseragentAppliesOnlyOnThe.message: Inclusive: the useragent applies only on the domains in the list below

tipOneDomainPerLineYahooComGoogleComOr.message: One domain per line: yahoo.com, google.com — or all_urls for every site

tipMakesTheFakeSurviveTheReadBackChecksR.message: Use Chromium's real NavigatorUAData instance. The selected profile supplies the public values while native methods retain valid receiver checks.

tipTheFakeSurvivesTheClassicReadBackChec.message: Native NavigatorUAData instance with profile-aware values

tipBuildsTheSmallBrandListChromeItselfWo.message: Builds the small brand list Chrome itself would send for the faked version, instead of the fixed list most spoofers carry; off restores the fixed list

tipBrandListAndOrderDeriveFromTheFakedVe.message: Brand list and order derive from the faked version

tipCoreHighEntropyValuesAlwaysStayConsis.message: Core high-entropy values always stay consistent with the selected Chromium profile; this option additionally exposes model and form-factor details

tipAddModelAndFormFactorDetailsToTheCons.message: Add model and form-factor details to the consistent core values

tipSitesThatAskForExtraBrowserDetailsGet.message: Sites that ask for extra browser details get the REAL machine's answers — useful when a page may see through the fake on purpose; off keeps every detail consistent with the fake

tipExtraDetailsAnswerThisMachineRevealsT.message: Extra details answer this machine (reveals the fake)

tipRemovesBrowserPropertiesTheFakedBrows.message: Removes browser properties the faked browser should not have (a fake Chrome answers nothing for Firefox-only fields, a fake Firefox hides the Chrome button); off leaves the extras in place

tipExtrasTheFakedFamilyWouldNotHaveGetRe.message: Extras the faked family would not have get removed

tipAFakeFirefoxReportsTheShortVersionStr.message: A fake Firefox reports the short version string the real Firefox uses (a long, Chrome-shaped string would give the fake away); off keeps the long string everywhere

tipFirefoxFakesUseTheShortVersionString.message: Firefox fakes use the short version string

tipSitesCanInspectTheCodeBehindAChangedP.message: Sites can inspect the code behind a changed property — this makes our code answer like the browser's built-in code; off exposes our code to anyone who looks closely (testing aid)

tipChangedCodeAnswersLikeBuiltInCode.message: Changed code answers like built-in code

tipSitesCanAskHowManyCPUCoresAndHow.message: Sites can ask how many CPU cores and how much memory the device has — the fake answers with fixed, believable numbers instead of yours; off passes the real numbers through

tipCoresAndMemoryAnswerFixedFakeNumbers.message: Cores and memory answer fixed fake numbers

tipSitesThatRunAutomationToolsBotsTestDr.message: Sites that run automation tools (bots, test drivers) carry a flag pages read — this answers false while the fake is on, like a normal session; off passes the real flag through

tipTheAutomationFlagAnswersFalseWhileThe.message: The automation flag answers false while the fake is on

tipAPageAnswerWhoseTextIsExactlyThisBrow.message: A page answer whose text is exactly this browser's real identity readback is a test trap — this switch lets such a page-level echo report the fake instead; off hands the real string through, and any other page text is never touched

tipAPageAnswerThatIsExactlyTheRealIdenti.message: A page answer that is exactly the real identity reads as the fake

tipSitesRunPartsOfTheirPageInHiddenBoxes.message: Sites run parts of their page in hidden boxes before our script can arrive there — this switch sends the fake ahead of time in the page's answer, so even their first script reads it; off uses the slower round trip

tipEveryFrameReportsTheFakeBeforeItsFirs.message: Every frame reports the fake before its first script runs

tipHiddenBoxesOnAPageReportTheFakeLike.message: Hidden boxes on a page report the fake like the main page; off narrows everything to the main page only, so no layer contradicts another

tipFramesOfTheTabCarryTheFakeToo.message: Frames of the tab carry the fake too

tipSitesBuildLockedBoxesAndReadTheIdenti.message: Sites build locked boxes and read the identity inside them the moment the box is created; this switch hands the fake over inside that create action itself; off leaves locked boxes untouched

tipLockedFramesGetTheFakeTheMomentTheyAr.message: Locked frames get the fake the moment they are built

tipNormallyTheFakeTravelsInvisiblyThisDe.message: Normally the fake travels invisibly; this debug switch leaves its trace readable in the browser's timeline for checking — keep it off for daily use

tipTheServerTimingPayloadStaysReadableTe.message: The Server-Timing payload stays readable (testing aid)

tipTheFakeSpeaksTheLanguageListBelowPage.message: The fake speaks the language list below: pages get the chosen language instead of this browser's real one; off leaves language untouched — a language switch is visible on every page

tipLanguageHeaderAndNavigatorLanguagesMo.message: Language header and navigator.languages move together

tipTheLanguageListUsedWhenMatchLanguageI.message: The language list used when match-language is on: comma separated in order of importance, first entry is the main language (en-US, en); up to eight entries

tipOpenTheCustomDomainsViewWhereTheGloba.message: Open the custom domains view: where the global useragent applies

tipOpenTheCustomUseragentsViewEditorSave.message: Open the custom useragents view: editor, saved strings and the page detection

tipOpenTheHardeningPanelAntiDetectionSpo.message: Open the hardening panel: anti-detection spoof rules

tipExportSettingsAsAJSONFile.message: Export settings as a JSON file

tipImportSettingsFromAJSONFile.message: Import settings from a JSON file

tipFactoryResetClearsAllSettingsRulesAnd.message: Factory reset: clears all settings, rules and the toolbar icon state

tipInterfaceLanguage.message: Choose the popup language independently of the spoofed browser language
